text:
Anya: Heads-up — AuroraASIC wants to run a joint perf/W + throughput sweep next Tue (they suggested 2026-06-09). They want a short plan from us for kernel tuning knobs, telemetry metrics we need, and what artifacts we share for a public joint note.

Kevin: Great. Can they run our test harness or do we run on their infra? We should lock the exact model variants and sequence lengths.

Aurora CI Bot: @Anya I can schedule the CI job if you give me a test-config YAML. Defaults: batch_sizes=[1,4,8], seq_lens=[128,512,1024], reps=3.

Anya: Kevin — they prefer to run on their hardware but with our harness to ensure parity. So we need a container and a small shim. Oliver, can bench team produce a lightweight docker / runbook?

Oliver: Yep. I'll put together a docker image with our runtime + kv cache disabled for the baseline. Plan to collect: power (W), p95 latency, tokens/s, GPU temp, and kernel logs. Will also include a small script to upload telemetry to our private S3 bucket.

Sam: Before data transfer, legal needs clarity on what we can publish. If Aurora wants a joint announcement, we need an approved CSV with aggregated perf numbers and a short methodology paragraph. Also confirm if any raw telemetry is covered by their NDA.

Emily: I can take point on the PR angle and the marketplace badge. Suggest we agree on two publishable configs: "latency-optimized" and "cost-optimized (perf/W)". That gives marketing clear hooks.

Kevin: Technical ask: we should propose a kernel sweep matrix. Idea: vary warp_size (simulated param), activation-tiling (A1/A2), and quantization level (fp16, int8, q4_nop). We should also test with batching disabled vs batching=8 for throughput curves.

Oliver: Draft kernel sweep (short):
```
# kernel_sweep.csv
warp_size,activation_tiling,quant,batched
32,A1,fp16,1
32,A2,fp16,8
64,A1,int8,1
64,A2,q4_nop,8
```
I'll run the first dry-run on our staging rig Wed morning and post results.

Aurora CI Bot: Scheduling confirmation: test-config received. Job queued on aurora-ci-12 for Tue 04:00 UTC. ETA for logs: +2h after completion.

Anya: Two operational asks: 1) we need a short dashboard template in Console showing perf/W vs throughput across configs, 2) alert thresholds for regressions (e.g., tokens/s drop >10% or perf/W drop >8%). Oliver can you add the dashboard widgets and the eval hooks?

Oliver: Will add widgets: tokens/s (line), perf_per_watt (bar), p95 latency (heatmap). Eval hooks: baseline snapshot + auto-regression check; if check fails send to #eng-runtime and cc @Kevin.

Sam: I'll loop in legal with the proposed publishable configs and a suggested attribution blurb. Please don't share customer data; only synthetic/bench model runs.

Emily: For the marketplace badge, marketing needs a short blurb and a logo from Aurora. I'll request their brand kit. Also, let's agree on a 48-hour embargo window post-run so we can validate numbers.

Kevin: Question for Aurora: do they have power meters per GPU or node-level? Node-level is fine but we should annotate that in methodology. Also record ambient room temp.

Aurora CI Bot: Aurora reply: "We have per-GPU inline sensors + rack PDU. We'll export both. Ambient logged by BMS."

Anya: OK. Action list: (1) Oliver — docker + runbook + dashboard templates (due Mon EOD). (2) Kevin — kernel sweep matrix + test-config review (due Mon noon). (3) Emily — marketing assets request + embargo coord (due Mon EOD). (4) Sam — legal clearance draft for publishable CSV (due Mon EOD). (5) Aurora CI Bot — run Tue, post logs.

Oliver: I'll attach the runbook draft here after the staging dry-run. For the shim, use this run command to reproduce locally:
```
docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/data:/data redwood/bench:dev \ 
  --model redispatched-gpt-medium --batch 8 --seq 512 --sweep-file kernel_sweep.csv --upload /tmp/artifacts
```
Make sure to set REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=private-s3 in env.

Emily: FYI — suggested headline options: "Redwood + AuroraASIC: 2x perf/W at parity latency" or "Redwood runtime tuned for AuroraASIC delivers 30% throughput boost" — we'll pick after numbers land.

Anya: Perfect. If no objections I'll close this thread after Oliver posts the runbook and Kevin does the review. :+1:

Kevin: No objections. Excited to see how the q4_nop path behaves on Aurora silicon.

Aurora CI Bot: Run completed: logs uploaded to s3://redwood-partner-aurora/1987654321/logs.tar.gz (link: https://s3.example/1987654321/logs.tar.gz)

Oliver: I'll start parsing; will post a short summary and attach the CSV of aggregated numbers within the hour.

Sam: Thanks all — once I see the summary I'll start the legal publish checklist.

Emily: Nice work — keep updates coming.

Anya: Closing notes: remember to tag any public art with both companies and include methodology. We'll sync on a quick 20m call Tue 10:30 UTC if needed.
